# Thermoelectric Conversion Module

A thermoelectric conversion module comprises a module body and a heat transfer portion.

The module body consists of multiple thermoelectric conversion module substrates. Each substrate features a flexible insulating base with either a P-type or N-type thermoelectric element mounted on one of its surfaces. A P-type element consists of a P-type thermoelectric layer paired with two connection electrodes that are electrically linked to it. Similarly, an N-type element comprises an N-type thermoelectric layer connected to its own pair of connection electrodes. These substrates are positioned so that the orientation of the connection electrodes matches the orientation of the insulating bases across the arrangement.

The heat transfer portion is positioned adjacent to at least one connection electrode on the module body. This component serves multiple functions: it applies pressure to the substrates along their arrangement direction, and it either conducts heat into the module body or draws heat away from it.

Two key performance parameters define this heat transfer portion:

First, its thermal conductivity must reach a minimum of 10 W/mK.

Second, when the heat transfer portion compresses the substrates along their arrangement direction, the resulting normal stress—measured perpendicular to the insulating base's surface—must be at least 0.01 MPa.

# Thermoelectric Conversion Module: Structural Configuration and Thermal Performance Requirements

## Module Body Composition

The thermoelectric conversion module body is constructed from a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates assembled together to form a unified structure. Each individual substrate within this assembly incorporates a flexible insulating substrate as its foundational component. Mounted upon these flexible insulating substrates are thermoelectric conversion elements, which may be of either P-type or N-type semiconductor material, depending on the specific design requirements of the module. In conjunction with these thermoelectric elements, each substrate is also equipped with corresponding connection electrodes that serve to establish the necessary electrical pathways for the thermoelectric conversion process.

## Substrate Arrangement Configuration

The multiple thermoelectric conversion module substrates are arranged in a specific spatial configuration such that the orientation of the connection electrodes corresponds with, and aligns along, the same directional axis as the insulating substrates throughout the entire assembly. This consistent directional alignment across all substrates within the module ensures structural coherence and enables uniform electrical and thermal characteristics throughout the assembled module body. This arrangement strategy is critical for maintaining consistent performance across the entire thermoelectric conversion module.

## Heat Transfer Portion Placement and Function

A heat transfer portion is strategically positioned on the side of the module body that is proximate to at least one of the connection electrodes. This heat transfer portion serves a dual functional purpose within the overall module architecture. First, it acts as a mechanical pressing mechanism, applying compressive force to the substrates along the arrangement direction, thereby ensuring the multiple thermoelectric conversion module substrates remain securely pressed together and maintain proper physical contact throughout the assembly. Second, and simultaneously, this heat transfer portion facilitates the essential functions of heat transfer and heat dissipation, allowing thermal energy to be efficiently conducted through or away from the module structure as required by the thermoelectric conversion process.

## Thermal Conductivity Requirement

To ensure that the module achieves efficient thermal performance, the heat transfer portion must be composed of, or otherwise possess, a thermal conductivity value of no less than 10 W/mK. This minimum thermal conductivity threshold is essential for enabling the heat transfer portion to adequately conduct thermal energy across the module structure without introducing significant thermal resistance that would otherwise compromise the overall efficiency of the thermoelectric conversion process.

## Mechanical Pressing Force Specification

In addition to the thermal conductivity requirement, the heat transfer portion must also satisfy a specific mechanical performance criterion when it is engaged in pressing the thermoelectric conversion module substrates together. Specifically, the pressing action exerted by the heat transfer portion must generate a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa, with this stress being applied in a direction perpendicular to the surface of the insulating substrate. This minimum normal stress requirement ensures that sufficient compressive force is maintained between adjacent substrates within the assembly, thereby guaranteeing reliable mechanical contact and consistent thermal interface performance across the entire module body during operation.

# Thermoelectric Conversion Module with Enhanced Heat Transfer Structure

## Background of the Invention

Thermoelectric conversion modules, which utilize the Seebeck effect for power generation or the Peltier effect for heating/cooling applications, have traditionally faced significant challenges in efficiently managing heat transfer to and from their active elements. Conventional rigid thermoelectric modules, while functional in flat, planar applications, often struggle to maintain adequate thermal contact when installed on curved, irregular, or dynamically changing surfaces—a limitation that substantially reduces their practical utility in real-world applications such as automotive exhaust systems, industrial piping, wearable devices, and other non-planar heat sources.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these longstanding challenges through a novel flexible thermoelectric conversion module design that incorporates a dedicated heat transfer portion engineered to optimize thermal contact while maintaining structural integrity.

### Module Configuration

The thermoelectric conversion module of this invention comprises a plurality of P-type and N-type thermoelectric elements arranged in an alternating pattern on flexible insulating substrates. This arrangement allows the module to conform to various surface geometries, significantly expanding the range of potential applications compared to conventional rigid designs. The P-type and N-type elements are electrically connected in series or parallel configurations to generate the desired voltage and current characteristics for power generation, or to enable controlled heating and cooling when operated in Peltier mode.

The flexibility of the insulating substrates—which may be composed of polymer films, flexible ceramics, or composite materials—enables the module to be installed on curved surfaces, wrapped around cylindrical objects such as pipes, or integrated into flexible systems that must accommodate movement or thermal expansion during operation.

### The Heat Transfer Portion

A key innovation of this invention lies in the dedicated heat transfer portion, which is specifically designed to press the insulating substrates together in their arrangement direction. This pressing action serves two critical functions simultaneously: ensuring intimate thermal contact between the substrates and their associated heat sources or heat sinks, and maintaining the mechanical integrity of the flexible module structure during operation.

The heat transfer portion is characterized by two essential physical properties that distinguish it from conventional thermal interface materials:

**High Thermal Conductivity**: The heat transfer portion exhibits a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or higher. This relatively high thermal conductivity value ensures that heat can be efficiently conducted through the heat transfer portion to or from the thermoelectric elements, minimizing thermal resistance losses that would otherwise degrade the overall conversion efficiency of the module. Materials achieving this thermal conductivity threshold may include various thermally conductive polymers, metal-filled composites, graphite-based materials, or other engineered thermal interface materials.

**Controlled Normal Stress**: The heat transfer portion applies a normal stress of 0.01 MPa or higher in the direction perpendicular to the substrate surface. This mechanical pressing force is critical for eliminating air gaps and microscopic voids at the interface between the substrates and adjacent thermal surfaces, which would otherwise significantly impede heat transfer due to the low thermal conductivity of air. By maintaining this minimum stress threshold, the invention ensures consistent and reliable thermal contact even as the module flexes or as thermal cycling occurs during operation.

### Advantages and Technical Effects

The combination of these two specified parameters—thermal conductivity and normal stress—works synergistically to address the fundamental challenge of heat transfer in flexible thermoelectric modules. Without adequate thermal conductivity, even perfect mechanical contact would fail to efficiently transfer heat. Conversely, without sufficient normal stress, even a highly thermally conductive material might fail to maintain the intimate contact necessary for effective heat transfer, particularly as the module undergoes mechanical stress from bending, thermal expansion, or vibration.

This dual-parameter approach ensures that:

1. **Thermal Efficiency is Maximized**: The high thermal conductivity threshold minimizes thermal resistance losses, allowing more heat to reach or be extracted from the thermoelectric elements, thereby improving the temperature differential across the module and increasing overall conversion efficiency.

2. **Mechanical Stability is Preserved**: The applied normal stress maintains consistent contact pressure between components, preventing degradation of thermal contact over time due to material settling, thermal cycling, or mechanical vibration.

3. **Flexibility is Maintained**: Unlike rigid clamping mechanisms that would compromise the module's ability to conform to curved surfaces, the heat transfer portion is designed to work in conjunction with the flexible substrate arrangement, allowing the entire assembly to maintain its adaptive properties while still ensuring adequate thermal contact.

4. **Reliability is Enhanced**: The combination of proper thermal conductivity and mechanical pressure reduces the likelihood of thermal fatigue, delamination, or other failure modes that commonly affect thermoelectric modules subjected to repeated thermal cycling or mechanical stress.

### Applications

This invention finds particular utility in applications where thermoelectric modules must be installed on non-planar surfaces or in environments subject to vibration, thermal cycling, or mechanical stress. Potential applications include waste heat recovery systems for automotive exhaust pipes, industrial process heat recovery from curved or irregular surfaces, wearable thermoelectric generators that must conform to body contours, and various other applications where the combination of flexibility and efficient heat transfer is essential for practical implementation.

By addressing both the mechanical and thermal aspects of the heat transfer challenge simultaneously, this invention represents a significant advancement in the practical deployment of thermoelectric conversion technology across a broader range of real-world applications than previously possible with conventional rigid module designs.

# Understanding MPa: The Megapascal Unit

MPa, or megapascal, is a unit of pressure and stress commonly used in engineering, materials science, and construction. It represents one million pascals (Pa), the SI-derived unit of pressure. Since one pascal is defined as one newton per square meter (N/m²), one megapascal equals one million newtons per square meter, or equivalently, one newton per square millimeter (N/mm²).

## Why MPa Matters

The megapascal is particularly useful because many engineering applications involve pressures and stresses too large to conveniently express in pascals alone. Using MPa simplifies calculations and communication in fields where forces are substantial relative to the areas involved.

## Common Applications

**Construction and Materials Engineering**
MPa is frequently used to specify the compressive strength of concrete. For example, standard residential concrete might have a strength rating of 20-30 MPa, while high-strength structural concrete can exceed 40-80 MPa. This measurement tells engineers how much load the material can withstand before failure.

**Metal and Alloy Properties**
The tensile strength, yield strength, and hardness of metals are often reported in MPa. Steel, for instance, typically has a tensile strength ranging from 400 to over 2000 MPa depending on its composition and treatment.

**Hydraulic and Pneumatic Systems**
Pressure ratings for hydraulic systems, pipelines, and pressure vessels are commonly expressed in MPa, helping engineers determine appropriate materials and safety margins.

**Tire Pressure and Industrial Equipment**
While tire pressure is often measured in other units like PSI or bar in everyday contexts, MPa appears in technical specifications for industrial machinery and high-pressure equipment.

## Conversion Context

To put MPa in perspective:
- 1 MPa ≈ 145.04 PSI (pounds per square inch)
- 1 MPa = 10 bar
- 1 MPa = 1,000,000 Pa

## Conclusion

The megapascal serves as a practical bridge between the theoretical SI unit of pressure and real-world engineering demands. Its widespread use across construction, manufacturing, and materials testing makes it an essential unit for professionals who need to communicate stress and pressure values clearly and efficiently. Understanding MPa is fundamental for anyone working in structural engineering, materials science, or related technical fields.

# PATENT SPECIFICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**THERMOELECTRIC MODULE WITH MULTI-SUBSTRATE ARCHITECTURE AND COMPRESSIVE HEAT TRANSFER INTERFACE ASSEMBLY**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to thermoelectric conversion devices, and more particularly to a thermoelectric module comprising a plurality of substrates carrying P-type and N-type thermoelectric elements, interconnected by conductive electrodes, and incorporating a heat transfer mechanism configured to apply compressive normal stress across substrate interfaces while satisfying specified thermal conductivity and mechanical pressure thresholds to optimize thermal energy conversion efficiency and structural reliability.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Thermoelectric modules convert thermal energy directly into electrical energy (Seebeck effect) or electrical energy into a temperature differential (Peltier effect) through arrays of P-type and N-type semiconductor elements electrically connected in series and thermally connected in parallel between a heat source and heat sink.

[0003] Conventional thermoelectric modules typically employ a single pair of ceramic substrates sandwiching the thermoelectric element array, with element-to-substrate bonding accomplished via solder or brazing. Such designs suffer from several deficiencies:

(a) Thermal stress accumulation at solder joints due to coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between ceramic substrates, metallic electrodes, and semiconductor elements, leading to fatigue cracking and eventual electrical discontinuity;

(b) Inadequate thermal interface contact under varying operational temperatures, resulting in increased thermal contact resistance and degraded conversion efficiency;

(c) Difficulty in scaling modular architectures for stacked or cascaded thermoelectric configurations without introducing additional parasitic thermal resistance at each interface;

(d) Insufficient mechanical robustness under thermal cycling, particularly in high-temperature waste heat recovery applications exceeding 200°C.

[0004] Prior art attempts to address these issues, such as those employing rigid mechanical fasteners or adhesive bonding layers, fail to provide a self-adjusting compressive force capable of maintaining consistent thermal contact across the substrate stack throughout thermal expansion and contraction cycles, nor do they establish quantifiable performance thresholds correlating applied normal stress to achieved thermal conductivity at the interface.

[0005] There exists a need for a thermoelectric module architecture that accommodates multiple substrate pairs in a scalable configuration, maintains reliable electrical interconnection via robust electrode structures, and incorporates a compressive heat transfer mechanism engineered to satisfy defined minimum thermal conductivity and normal stress thresholds to ensure consistent performance across operating conditions.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0006] The present invention provides a thermoelectric module comprising:

(i) a plurality of substrates, each substrate supporting an array of alternating P-type and N-type thermoelectric elements;

(ii) a plurality of connection electrodes disposed on interior surfaces of the substrates, electrically interconnecting the P-type and N-type elements in a series circuit while providing thermally conductive pathways to the substrate surfaces;

(iii) a heat transfer mechanism disposed to mechanically engage and press the plurality of substrates together along a compression axis substantially perpendicular to the substrate planes, the heat transfer mechanism comprising a compressive biasing structure and an interposed thermal interface layer; and

(iv) wherein the heat transfer mechanism is configured such that the thermal interface achieves a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/m·K and the compressive biasing structure applies a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa across the substrate interface, in combination sufficient to minimize thermal contact resistance while accommodating differential thermal expansion between adjacent substrates during operation.

[0007] In accordance with certain embodiments, the compressive biasing structure comprises a spring-loaded assembly, a resilient conductive gasket, a Belleville washer stack, or a pneumatic/hydraulic bladder configured to maintain the specified normal stress threshold across a defined operational temperature range (e.g., -40°C to 300°C).

[0008] In further embodiments, the thermal interface layer comprises a compliant thermally conductive material selected from graphite sheet, liquid metal alloy, metal-filled silicone, or sintered metal particle layers, engineered to achieve the specified thermal conductivity threshold under the applied normal stress.

[0009] The module architecture permits stacking of multiple substrate-electrode-element assemblies in a modular fashion, with the heat transfer mechanism interposed at each substrate-to-substrate junction, enabling scalable thermoelectric arrays for cascaded power generation or multi-stage cooling applications.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0010] **FIG. 1** is a cross-sectional side view of a thermoelectric module according to a first embodiment, illustrating a stack of two substrate assemblies joined by a heat transfer mechanism.

[0011] **FIG. 2** is an exploded perspective view showing the arrangement of P-type and N-type thermoelectric elements, connection electrodes, and substrate layers.

[0012] **FIG. 3** is a detailed cross-sectional view of the heat transfer mechanism, depicting the compressive biasing structure and thermal interface layer.

[0013] **FIG. 4** is a schematic diagram illustrating the series electrical circuit formed by connection electrodes interconnecting P/N element pairs.

[0014] **FIG. 5** is a graph plotting achieved thermal conductivity (W/m·K) versus applied normal stress (MPa) for various thermal interface layer materials, demonstrating threshold compliance.

[0015] **FIG. 6** is a cross-sectional view of an alternative embodiment employing a multi-substrate stacked configuration with repeated heat transfer mechanisms at each junction.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### 1. General Architecture

[0016] Referring to FIG. 1, thermoelectric module **100** comprises a first substrate **110** and a second substrate **120**, each fabricated from an electrically insulating, thermally conductive ceramic material such as aluminum nitride (AlN), alumina (Al₂O₃), or beryllium oxide (BeO). Substrates **110**, **120** may alternatively comprise a direct-bonded copper (DBC) or active metal brazed (AMB) ceramic laminate to enhance in-plane thermal spreading.

[0017] Disposed upon the interior-facing surface of substrate **110** is an array of P-type thermoelectric elements **130** (e.g., bismuth telluride doped with antimony, Bi₂Te₃-Sb₂Te₃ alloys) and N-type thermoelectric elements **140** (e.g., bismuth telluride doped with selenium, Bi₂Te₃-Bi₂Se₃ alloys), arranged in alternating columnar fashion.

[0018] A plurality of connection electrodes **150** are patterned on the interior surfaces of substrates **110** and **120**, each electrode fabricated from a highly conductive metal (copper, silver, or nickel-plated copper) and configured to bridge adjacent P-type and N-type elements such that the elements are connected electrically in series while remaining thermally in parallel between the hot-side and cold-side substrates. Electrodes **150** are bonded to elements **130**, **140** via soldering, sintering, or diffusion bonding to minimize electrical and thermal contact resistance.

### 2. Heat Transfer Mechanism

[0019] The heat transfer mechanism **160**, illustrated in detail in FIG. 3, is interposed between substrate **120** and an adjacent substrate **170** (in multi-substrate embodiments) or between substrate **120** and an external heat sink/source (in single-stage embodiments). The mechanism **160** comprises:

(a) a **compressive biasing structure 161**, which may take the form of:
   - a plurality of coil springs distributed peripherally or centrally about the substrate interface;
   - a Belleville disc spring stack providing high force in a compact axial envelope;
   - a resilient conductive gasket formed of compressed expanded graphite or metal mesh;
   - a sealed pneumatic or hydraulic bladder charged to a predetermined pressure;

(b) a **thermal interface layer 162**, interposed directly between the mutually facing surfaces of substrates **120** and **170** (or heat sink), comprising a compliant material selected to conform to microscopic surface asperities and thereby reduce thermal contact resistance. Suitable materials include:
   - natural or synthetic graphite sheet (thermal conductivity ~150-400 W/m·K in-plane, ~5-25 W/m·K through-plane);
   - liquid metal alloys such as gallium-indium-tin (Galinstan) (thermal conductivity ~16-40 W/m·K);
   - silver- or aluminum-filled silicone elastomer pads (thermal conductivity ~10-15 W/m·K);
   - sintered silver or copper particle layers (thermal conductivity >20 W/m·K).

[0020] The compressive biasing structure **161** is configured and dimensioned such that, when the module **100** is assembled and constrained (e.g., by an enclosing housing, tie rods, or clamping frame **180**), the structure applies a continuous normal force **F** distributed across the substrate interface area **A**, yielding a normal stress σ = F/A of at least 0.01 MPa. This minimum stress threshold has been determined through experimentation to ensure adequate conformal contact between the thermal interface layer **162** and adjacent substrate surfaces across the operational temperature range, without exceeding the compressive strength limits of the thermoelectric elements **130**, **140** or inducing substrate fracture.

[0021] Simultaneously, the thermal interface layer **162**, under the applied normal stress, is configured to achieve an effective through-plane thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/m·K, as measured according to ASTM D5470 standard test method for thermal transmission properties of thermally conductive electrical insulation materials, or equivalent guarded hot-plate methodology.

[0022] FIG. 5 illustrates empirically the relationship between applied normal stress and achieved thermal conductivity for representative thermal interface materials, demonstrating that at the minimum specified normal stress of 0.01 MPa, each candidate material achieves the minimum thermal conductivity threshold of 10 W/m·K, with conductivity increasing asymptotically at higher applied stresses due to progressive elimination of micro-air-gaps at the mating surfaces.

### 3. Compliance and Threshold Rationale

[0023] The dual-threshold specification (≥10 W/m·K thermal conductivity in combination with ≥0.01 MPa normal stress) represents an engineering balance between:

(a) minimizing thermal contact resistance (R_contact = t/(k·A), where t is interface thickness, k is thermal conductivity, and A is contact area) to preserve the temperature differential (ΔT) available to the thermoelectric elements for power generation or to maximize cooling capacity in Peltier-mode operation; and

(b) limiting mechanical stress imparted to the brittle thermoelectric elements **130**, **140**, which typically exhibit compressive strength limits on the order of 50-100 MPa but may suffer microcracking at their solder joint interfaces under repeated thermal cycling if excessive normal stress is applied.

[0024] It has been found that maintaining normal stress at or above 0.01 MPa

# PATENT ABSTRACT

## Title
**Thermoelectric Device with Flexible Substrate Configuration and High Thermal Conductivity Pressure-Applying Heat Transfer Portion**

## Abstract

A thermoelectric device is disclosed comprising a pair of flexible insulating substrates disposed opposite one another, a plurality of thermoelectric elements including P-type thermoelectric elements and N-type thermoelectric elements arranged alternately between the flexible insulating substrates, connection electrodes disposed on facing surfaces of the flexible insulating substrates and electrically connecting the P-type thermoelectric elements and the N-type thermoelectric elements in series, wherein the connection electrodes are aligned in a first direction, and a heat transfer portion disposed on at least one outer surface of the flexible insulating substrates, the heat transfer portion being configured to apply pressure to the flexible insulating substrates and having a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or greater. The flexible nature of the insulating substrates enables the thermoelectric device to conform to curved or irregular surfaces, while the heat transfer portion simultaneously provides mechanical pressure to maintain intimate contact between the device and an adjacent heat source or heat sink and provides efficient thermal pathways, thereby improving thermoelectric conversion efficiency and structural reliability across varied application environments including wearable devices, automotive components, and industrial equipment.

---

## CLAIMS

**Claim 1** (Independent Claim)

A thermoelectric device comprising:

a first flexible insulating substrate and a second flexible insulating substrate disposed to face each other;

a plurality of thermoelectric elements disposed between the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate, the plurality of thermoelectric elements comprising a plurality of P-type thermoelectric elements and a plurality of N-type thermoelectric elements alternately arranged;

a plurality of connection electrodes disposed on at least one of a surface of the first flexible insulating substrate facing the second flexible insulating substrate and a surface of the second flexible insulating substrate facing the first flexible insulating substrate, the plurality of connection electrodes electrically connecting the plurality of P-type thermoelectric elements and the plurality of N-type thermoelectric elements to each other, wherein the plurality of connection electrodes are arranged along a first direction; and

a heat transfer portion disposed on an outer surface of at least one of the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate,

wherein the heat transfer portion is configured to apply pressure toward the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate, and

wherein the heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or more.

**Claim 2** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the heat transfer portion comprises an elastic member configured to apply the pressure by elastic restoring force.

**Claim 3** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the first direction in which the plurality of connection electrodes are arranged corresponds to a longitudinal direction of the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate.

**Claim 4** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the heat transfer portion comprises at least one material selected from the group consisting of a metal, a metal alloy, a graphite sheet, and a thermally conductive polymer composite.

**Claim 5** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the thermal conductivity of the heat transfer portion is in a range of 10 W/mK to 500 W/mK.

**Claim 6** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate each independently comprise a polymer film selected from the group consisting of polyimide, polyethylene terephthalate, and polyethylene naphthalate.

**Claim 7** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the plurality of connection electrodes comprise a first connection electrode disposed on the first flexible insulating substrate and a second connection electrode disposed on the second flexible insulating substrate, and

wherein the first connection electrode and the second connection electrode are electrically connected to opposite ends of each of the plurality of thermoelectric elements.

**Claim 8** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, wherein the heat transfer portion is configured to apply the pressure in a direction substantially perpendicular to a plane defined by the first flexible insulating substrate.

**Claim 9** (Dependent)

The thermoelectric device of claim 1, further comprising an adhesive layer disposed between the heat transfer portion and the outer surface of at least one of the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate.

**Claim 10** (Independent Claim - Method)

A method of manufacturing a thermoelectric device, the method comprising:

preparing a first flexible insulating substrate and a second flexible insulating substrate;

forming a plurality of connection electrodes on at least one of the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate, the plurality of connection electrodes being arranged along a first direction;

disposing a plurality of P-type thermoelectric elements and a plurality of N-type thermoelectric elements alternately between the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate such that the plurality of P-type thermoelectric elements and the plurality of N-type thermoelectric elements are electrically connected via the plurality of connection electrodes;

disposing a heat transfer portion on an outer surface of at least one of the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate, the heat transfer portion having a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or more; and

configuring the heat transfer portion to apply pressure toward the first flexible insulating substrate and the second flexible insulating substrate.

# Patent Claim

**Claim 1:**

A thermoelectric conversion module comprising:

a first substrate and a second substrate disposed opposite to each other, each of said first substrate and said second substrate having an inner surface facing one another and defining a gap therebetween;

a plurality of thermoelectric elements including at least one p-type thermoelectric element and at least one n-type thermoelectric element, said plurality of thermoelectric elements being arranged in an array between said inner surface of said first substrate and said inner surface of said second substrate;

a plurality of first electrodes disposed on said inner surface of said first substrate, each of said plurality of first electrodes being electrically connected to at least one end of a corresponding thermoelectric element of said plurality of thermoelectric elements;

a plurality of second electrodes disposed on said inner surface of said second substrate, each of said plurality of second electrodes being electrically connected to an opposite end of said corresponding thermoelectric element, said plurality of first electrodes and said plurality of second electrodes being arranged such that said p-type thermoelectric element and said n-type thermoelectric element adjacent thereto are electrically connected in series alternately through said plurality of first electrodes and said plurality of second electrodes to form a plurality of thermoelectric element pairs connected in series;

wherein at least one of said plurality of first electrodes and said plurality of second electrodes is provided, on a surface thereof facing said corresponding thermoelectric element, with a heat transfer portion interposed between said at least one of said plurality of first electrodes and said plurality of second electrodes and said corresponding thermoelectric element, said heat transfer portion being formed of a compressible material having elasticity such that said heat transfer portion is compressed by a compressive force applied in a stacking direction of said first substrate, said plurality of thermoelectric elements, and said second substrate when said thermoelectric conversion module is assembled;

wherein said heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of not less than 1 W/(m·K) in a compressed state under said compressive force; and

wherein said heat transfer portion exhibits a normal stress of not less than 0.1 MPa and not more than 10 MPa when compressed by 10% of an initial thickness thereof in said stacking direction,

whereby said heat transfer portion absorbs dimensional variations among said plurality of thermoelectric elements and unevenness of said inner surface of said first substrate and said inner surface of said second substrate, thereby ensuring uniform thermal and electrical contact between said plurality of thermoelectric elements and said plurality of first electrodes and said plurality of second electrodes while suppressing thermal resistance at an interface therebetween.
